Hi Alice / team — great working session earlier. Below are the technical notes and our first-pass recommendations based on the traffic CSV you shared and the models you plan to run. I also included actionable configuration snippets that you can share with your infra team.

Quick assumptions (from your CSV + call):
- Baseline 15 qps sustained
- Peak 120 qps sustained for 10 minutes (worst-case)
- Embeddings call: ~40ms on A100-80GB equiv (batching dependent)
- Reranker call: ~180ms on A100-80GB equiv (single-request latency)

Sizing recommendation (first pass):
- Baseline pool: 4 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (expected concurrency: embeddings batching yields ~60 qps per GPU; reranker concurrent capacity ~8-10 requests per GPU depending on model size).
- Burst headroom: keep an autoscaling buffer of +6 GPUs to cover 120 qps bursts when batching is suboptimal; target scale-up goal to add headroom within 60–90s for short promotional bursts.
- Concurrency limits: enforce per-GPU concurrency for non-batched reranker path (10 reqs/GPU) and allow higher for embeddings with batching (target batch size 32, but allow dynamic batching up to 64 for longer tails).
- Queue sizing: configure an internal request queue with capacity to hold ~2 minutes of peak traffic (120 qps * 120s = 14,400 requests); however, we recommend a soft limit and fast-fail/backpressure to upstream clients after queue depth > 8k to avoid latency tail risk. Use priority tiers to prefer personalized search requests over low-priority background enrichment.

Autoscaling policy suggestion:
- Primary trigger: queue depth + GPU utilization hybrid. Scale up when queue depth > 30% of configured queue capacity OR GPU util > 70% for 30s.
- Scale-down: when queue depth < 10% and GPU util < 40% for 5m.
- Warm pools: maintain a minimum of 2 hot GPUs in every AZ for immediate low-latency requests.

Routing & fallback: 
- SDK routing: include a "route_hint" flag in client SDK requests. Default route goes to dedicated pool. If dedicated pool rejects due to queue overflow, SDK retries to Redwood-hosted model endpoint (fallback tier) with a trace header so we can attribute costs.
- Auth: use short-lived API keys for service-to-service calls and mTLS between VPC peered nodes for control plane. Console and admin access via SAML SSO. KMS integration: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; we'll exchange IAM role ARNs to enable envelope encryption.

Structured output / tool-calling guidance:
- For any tool-calling flows, limit max tokens in model responses and use schema enforcement on the server side to validate outputs. Prefer function-calls for deterministic structured extraction to reduce downstream parsing errors.
- If you execute external enrichment (e.g., callouts to product DB), do it asynchronously for best latency. Return placeholders in real-time path and populate via background job if necessary.

Embeddings & reranker pattern:
- Maintain an embedding cache for frequently searched queries (TTL 1h). Use vector DB with approximate nearest neighbor indexes (HNSW) sharded by tenant.
- Reranker: run as a second-stage synchronous call for top-K candidates; for cost control consider a cheap lightweight scorer to prune before calling the large reranker.

Operational notes:
- Monitoring: expose per-route latency, per-model token counts, queue depth, and per-GPU utilization to your Grafana.
- Cost controls: set per-route quotas and automatic throttles during extended promotion runs.

Next steps (action items):
1) Marissa: share updated PoC MOP and procurement checklist (we'll include channel for KMS role exchange).
2) Alice: send the signed PO / procurement timeline if you want us to wire reserved capacity timelines.
3) Neha + Aditya: schedule a short validation run during next promotion window to validate autoscaler behavior (we can spin a canary test in a staging VPC).

I've attached a high-level network diagram and the example autoscaling JSON config snippet. Happy to walk through any of the recommended numbers in a quick call.
